evidence: Specific: the find list carries per-tool 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' chips (green when collectable now, grey when later), and the tool page calendar marks Wednesday/Saturday library sessions as 'Open' (dots on 375) - structure that comes from this product's one-of-each stock and few-hours desk.
Specific: copy-led details (deposit returned, 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower', 'What happens next' at the community centre) are this library's.

Generic: the visual layer is a stock form-and-card system - white bordered cards on a pale grey-green ground, one dark green button colour, a bold geometric sans for headings; swap the words and a clinic, a room-booking or a council service would wear it unchanged.
Generic: every tool card shows the same wrench glyph in a pale green square (find, 1280-light and 375-light), so the one image slot does no identifying work.

unfinished: Ten identical wrench placeholder tiles on the find list stand in for tool images (items-ladder-3m/default/1280-light, 375-light).
Browser-default date input showing 'yyyy/mm/dd' and a native select in the filters panel, with the two fields' labels misaligned (items-ladder-3m/filters-open/768-light).

Right half of the content column empty on tool, confirm and done at 1280/1440: forms and text stop at ~700px while cards span 1088px (tool default/1280-light, confirm default/1280-light, done default/1280-light).
Footer band stops short, leaving a bare grey band below it on short pages at 1280 (basket default/1280-light, done default/1280-light).
Headings differ from body only by size and weight; no typographic moment, imagery or drawn device anywhere in the flow; the only identity is the name and a small wrench in the header.
Basket session options break into one full-width row plus five cramped three-line cards at 1280 (basket default/1280-light).
evidence: First viewport of find at 1280: heading, paragraph, search bar, then a grid of identical bordered cards - orderly and legible, nothing to look at beyond the green chips.
After scrolling: an 'Opening times' paragraph and a one-line footer; the done page confirms with a plain key-value table and an outline button, no moment of reassurance.
It is clean and calm and dark mode is carefully themed, but it reads as a well-built default form rather than something the volunteers would be proud of as their library's face.
